title: Quota is check-then-consume with the consume after the upstream round trip: overshoot up to MaxConnections x unbounded tokens, and aborted/errored streams are never metered at all

verified_lines.quota_check_pure_read: backend/internal/quota/quota.go:158 `qm.db.Where("id IN ? AND enabled = ?", ids, true).Find(&rows)` and :173 `if r.LimitValue > 0 && used >= r.LimitValue {` - Check (148-179) performs no write/reservation
verified_lines.check_call_site: backend/internal/gateway/gateway.go:419 `if ok3, over := s.qm.Check(snap, apiKey.ID, ap.alias); !ok3 {`
verified_lines.consume_after_relay: backend/internal/gateway/gateway.go:614 `s.qm.Consume(snap, ap.keyID, ap.alias, usage.Prompt, usage.Completion)` (non-stream, after c.Data at :612) and :768, gated by :767 `if ap.status == "ok" || ap.status == "blocked" {` (stream end)
verified_lines.aborted_stream_unmetered: backend/internal/gateway/gateway.go:719-727: `if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {` ... :725 `ap.status = "error"`, :726 `return frFatal` - fails the :767 gate, Consume never called; same for upstream error events :660-666; non-stream disconnect chain :557-561 (frRetry) -> :472-476 (502, no Consume)
verified_lines.window_bounds: gateway.go:498 `timeout := time.Duration(snap.General.DefaultTimeoutSeconds) * time.Second` with default 120 at settings.go:31; streams skip any total timeout (gateway.go:492-505, :496-497)
verified_lines.admission_ceiling: gateway.go:195 `if int64(snap.General.MaxConnections) > 0 && s.mx.Conns() >= int64(snap.General.MaxConnections) {` - global, default 1000 at settings.go:32; no seeded rate-limit rules or quotas exist (grep finds only tests); rate limits bound requests/window, not token delta
verified_lines.max_tokens_uncapped: backend/internal/adapter/adapter.go:462-466 forwards client max_tokens verbatim (`payload["max_tokens"] = cr.MaxTokens`); adapter.go:648 `maxInt(cr.MaxTokens, 4096)` is only a floor; non-stream body read capped at 16<<20 (gateway.go:557), stream unbounded
verified_lines.reset_branch_assignment: quota.go:196-198 `if now.After(q.ResetAt) { qm.db.Model(&model.Quota{}).Where("id = ?", q.ID).Updates(map[string]any{"used_value": delta, "reset_at": NextReset(q.Period, now)})` - assignment, and q comes from the ~3s-stale snapshot (quota.go:184 matchQuotas(snap,...); HotReloadSeconds=3 settings.go:32), so it can clobber even the ticker reset at quota.go:257-258
verified_lines.degrade_not_rechecked: gateway.go:421-427 switches ap.alias to over.DegradeAlias after Check and proceeds without re-running Check against the new alias's quotas

impact: The quota control - the operator's only billing guardrail against an API-key holder - is both overshootable and bypassable. (1) TOCTOU: the Check->Consume window is the entire upstream round trip (120s non-stream, unbounded stream), so one burst of up to MaxConnections=1000 concurrent requests admitted at used_value < limit spends up to 1000x the per-request allowance, with per-request token delta itself attacker-shaped (uncapped max_tokens, unbounded stream) - a '1 request/day' key bills thousands of full-length completions to the operator's provider keys. (2) Bypass: any stream ending in a read error (including attacker-induced via client disconnect, which cancels the ctx propagated to the upstream body at gateway.go:496/515) returns frFatal at :726 with status "error", failing the :767 gate, so generated-and-billed tokens are never added to used_value - an infinite loop of 'start large completion, disconnect at N KB' leaves the quota counter permanently at zero. The same applies to non-stream disconnects (all retries fail on the canceled ctx -> 502 path with no Consume). (3) Corruption: the expired-cycle branch at quota.go:197-198 assigns instead of increments, so concurrent consumers overwrite each other's usage (and stale-snapshot ResetAt extends the clobber window into the fresh cycle), under-counting even normal successful traffic.
exploit_sketch: Attack A (burst): with one valid key, fire ~1000 concurrent streaming requests with max_tokens=200000; all pass Check while used_value is still 0 (Consume runs only after full relay at gateway.go:614/:768), so all 1000 hit the upstream provider. Attack B (permanent zero-counter): loop `curl -N --max-time 1` streaming a long generation; after 1s the client disconnect cancels the request ctx, the upstream body read fails, scanner.Err() fires (gateway.go:719), ap.status="error" (:725), `return frFatal` (:726) fails the ok/blocked gate (:767), Consume is skipped - provider bills the partial generation while the key's quota counter never moves; repeat forever. Attack C (accounting loss): N concurrent requests completing within the expired-cycle (or stale-snapshot) window each run `used_value = delta` (quota.go:197-198), erasing all but the last request's usage.
recommendation: Reserve before forwarding with an atomic conditional update (`UPDATE quotas SET used_value = used_value + :est WHERE id = ? AND (used_value + :est) <= limit_value`, estimate via tokens.Count on the request body) fused into Check, reconciled with the real delta in Consume; make the lazy-reset branch increment-based (or transactional with a used_value=0 guard); meter aborted streams and error paths (Consume the accumulated usage before returning frFatal at :666/:726 and on the final 502 path), since the upstream already produced those tokens; enforce an operator-set per-alias max_tokens ceiling in adapter.BuildUpstreamRequest; re-run Check against DegradeAlias after the degrade switch (gateway.go:421-427).
mitigations_checked: quota.go:201 `UpdateColumn("used_value", gorm.Expr("used_value + ?", delta))` is atomic SQL for the non-reset branch (filer's claim correct); Check re-reads live DB rows (quota.go:158) so usage survives restarts; delta<=0 skipped (quota.go:192-194); global MaxConnections admission (gateway.go:195) caps burst size at 1000 but is not per-key and does not cap token delta; in-memory rate limiter counts requests at Allow time (quota.go:73) which would partially bound bursts, but no default rules are seeded (settings EnsureDefaults writes no rate-limit/quota rows); no CORS/TLS layer relevant; SQLite write serialization does not close the read-then-consume window; the EOF-without-finish stream case (gateway.go:728-732) is still metered, so that direction is over-counting, not exploitable.
verdict_reason: CONFIRMED as filed, severity high retained. All cited evidence lines are verbatim at the stated line numbers (quota.go:148/158/173/192-194/196-198/201, gateway.go:419/498/614/726/767-768, settings.go:31-32), re-read end-to-end against backend/internal/quota/quota.go and backend/internal/gateway/gateway.go. The causal chain holds with no missing mitigation: Check is a pure read, the only two Consume call sites in production code run strictly after the upstream round trip (grep verified: gateway.go:614 and :768 only), the window is 120s-to-unbounded, the sole admission control is the global 1000-connection gauge, max_tokens is client-controlled and uncapped in the adapter, and the ok/blocked status gate provably excludes every error/aborted path from metering. Privilege model is appropriate: the attacker is an authenticated key holder, and quota is precisely the control meant to constrain that principal's spend - bypassing it is an authed-but-severe cost-exhaustion control failure, which maps to high under the audit rules (not critical: no unauth RCE/authz-takeover/data-exfil; not medium: the control is fully bypassable with trivial tooling, not merely a defense-in-depth gap). Two minor imprecisions in the original text are noted and do not affect the verdict: 'overshoot effectively unlimited' is strictly true for streams while a non-stream burst is bounded per attempt by the 16 MiB response read (gateway.go:557); and provider billing of client-canceled generations is provider-dependent (most bill tokens produced to cancellation; the TOCTOU burst component requires no disconnect at all and is code-proven regardless).
